name: Haast's eagle
intro: Zib! New Zealand, 1300. Glorp just saw a shadow the size of a small plane sweep over the forest. Duck!
description: Haast's eagle was the largest eagle ever known. Females, the bigger sex, weighed around 10 to 18 kilograms, with a wingspan of up to about 3 metres and talons as big as a tiger's claws. It lived on New Zealand's South Island, where there were no land mammals except bats, and it was the top predator: it hunted moa, giant flightless birds many times its own weight, by diving on them at high speed. Its closest living relatives are much smaller eagles. When people arrived in New Zealand around 1300 and hunted the moa to extinction, the eagle lost its prey, and it died out soon after, around 1445.

terrain.value: Forest edges and scrubland where moa grazed
terrain.why: It hunted moa in open scrub and at forest edges, perching in trees to watch.

temperature.why: The South Island is cool, with frosty winters near the mountains.

humidity.why: Wet westerly winds bring lots of rain and cloud to the island.

oxygen.why: Ordinary air, like any other bird.

pressure.why: It soared from the coast up into the mountains, where the air is thinner.

hotspots.label: Snowy peaks

hotspots.label: Rain clouds
hotspots.fact: Winds off the sea drop lots of rain on this side of the island.

hotspots.label: Mountain foothills
hotspots.fact: The eagle soared from the coast into the mountains, where the air is thinner.

hotspots.label: Giant talon
hotspots.fact: A talon as big as a tiger's claw! Haast's eagle was the largest eagle that ever lived.

hotspots.fact: Females were bigger than males, weighing up to about 18 kg, with wings up to 3 m across.

hotspots.label: Moa bones
hotspots.fact: The eagle dived on moa many times its own weight. When people hunted the moa out, the eagle starved too.
